Re: LD 404 - An Act Regarding the Confidentiality of Certain Lottery Winner Identities
Senator Hickman, Representative Supica, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Veterans and Legal Affairs, thank you for the opportunity to provide information in opposition to LD 404 as currently written.
This initiative would prohibit the Bureau of Alcoholic Beverages and Lottery Operations (BABLO) from sharing the identity of an individual awarded a prize of $500,000 or more, unless that person provides written authorization, or to another state agency under specifically detailed in Title 8, Chapter 14-A of the Maine Revised Statutes.
In accordance with 22 M.R.S. Section 3104(16)(B), BABLO shares a monthly list of individuals with gross lottery and gambling winnings over $599 with the Office for Family Independence so that OFI can use that information solely to update its records and make eligibility determinations, where appropriate. This information-sharing arrangement enhances program integrity for OFI by helping to ensure that people who are not eligible for public assistance programs because of substantial lottery winnings are removed from those programs. As written, the bill would forbid this current practice and conflict with state and federal law. OFI requests that the bill be amended to allow the current information sharing agreement between BABLO and OFI to continue. Our suggestion would be to amend lines 6-8 as follows:
The bureau may disclose the identity of the person to another state agency solely for purposes authorized under federal or state law this chapter, and that state agency is prohibited from further disclosing the person's identity.
Please feel free to contact me if you have any questions during your deliberation of this bill and thank you for considering this information.
Sincerely,

Ian Yaffe, Director Office for Family Independence

Testimony ofRep. James Dill introducing
LD 404, An Act Regarding the Confidentiality of Certain Lottery Winner
Identities.
Before the Veterans and Legal Affairs Committee
Senator Hickman, Representative Supica and distinguished members of the Veterans and Legal
Affairs Committee, my name is Jim Dill, and I represent House District 26 and the communities of Bradley, Old Town and Penobscot Nation Voting District. l am here before you today to
present LD 404, An Act Regarding the Confidentiality of Certain Lottery Winner Identities.

This is a fairly straightforward bill, and it came to me by request of a constituent. lt requires that
the State not release publicly the name of a lottery winner winning more than $500,000, unless the winner agrees (possible amended language). The exceptions would be the normal releases to certain Departments which may have some claims against the winner, perhaps DHHS, etc.

The main reasons for this bill are safety and harassment concerns for the winner and their family.

Thank you for your time this afternoon. I would be happy to answer any questions you have for me.

Neither for Nor Against LD 404 An Act Regarding the Confidentiality of Certain Lottery Winners
Senator Hickman, Representative Supica, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Veterans and Legal Affairs: I am Louis Luchini and I'm the Director of the Bureau of Alcoholic Beverages and Lottery Operations. I'm here to testify neither for nor against LD 404, An Act
Regarding the Confidentiality of Certain Lottery Winners, but to provide additional information for the committee's consideration.
This bill provides that the identity of a person awarded a lottery prize of $500,000 or more is confidential unless the person awarded the prize gives written authorization to the bureau allowing the disclosure of that person's identity.
For background, the definition of person under 8 MRS �37l (5) includes an "individual,
association, corporation, limited liability company, limited partnership, partnership, club, trust,
estate..." Some Maine winners have used these options as a way to preserve confidentiality, however the method is imperfect, and the winner's identity may be discovered.
The Bureau completely understands a lottery winner's desire to remain anonymous. We believe
this is a policy decision for the Legislature, and should the bill move forward, we'll be ready to
implement the program as desired.
However, we do oppose one provision in the bill, which begins on line 6. The text states: "The bureau may disclose the identity of the person to another state agency solely for purposes
authorized under this chapter, and that state agency is prohibited from further disclosing the person's identity."
Our concern is that BABLO currently discloses the identity of winners to other state agencies for a reasons not specifically authorized under Chapter 14-A. For instance, BABLO discloses the
identities of winners of lottery prizes over $599 to Maine Revenue Services and the IRS for tax
purposes. We also have a Memorandum of Understanding with the Office for Family
Independence (OFI) within DHHS, to disclose the identities of certain winners. This is required
under 22 MRS �3104, sub�-16. OFI uses this information in determining eligibility for certain
programs, including MaineCare, SNAP and TANF.

Testimony of Shemia Bellows, Secretary of State Department of the Secretary of State

February 26, 2025

Testifying neither for nor against
L.D. 404 "An Act Regarding the Confidentiality of Certain Lottery Winner Identities"
Senator Hickman, Representative Supica and Members of the Joint Standing Committee on Veterans
and Legal Affairs, my name is Sl'161'11'12l Bellows, I live in Manchester, and I am the Secretary of State. I am speaking today neither for nor against L.D. 404, but instead to offer a friendly additional proposal
for the committee's consideration as an amendment.
The Department of the Secretary of State administers the Address Confidentiality Program (ACP).
ACP provides two important services to residents of the State of Maine who are victims of domestic
violence, sexual assault or stalking: a designated address for victims who have moved to a new location unknown to their abuser and first-class confidential mail forwarding service to that address.

This allows state and local agencies to contribute to the safety of domestic violence, sexual assault and stalking victims by denying abusers the opportunity to use public records as a means to violate the rights of others.

For this reason, we considered what would happen if an ACP participant were to win the lottery.
Would their anonymity be compromised? Are they shut out from participating in the chance to win the lottery because of their well-founded fear of being found by the person who abused or stalked them?

If the committee is amenable to it, we would suggest an addition to the bill to provide that the identity
of a person awarded a prize of any dollar amount is confidential if the person is enrolled in the Address Confidentiality Program.

Thank you for the opportunity to speak, and I am happy to answer any questions you may have.
